simple.meaning: אֲבֵדָה (ʼăbêdâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “concrete, something lost ; abstract, destruction , i.e. Hades.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 22:8. The surrounding context includes family.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲבֵדָה (H9) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֲבֵדָה (ʼăbêdâh) / H9 is traced through Exodus 22:8, Leviticus 5:22, Leviticus 5:23, Deuteronomy 22:3 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out whether or not he has put his hand on his neighbor’s goods.

timeline.evidenceText: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out whether or not he has put his hand on his neighbor’s goods.
So you shall do with his donkey. So you shall do with his garment. So you shall do with every lost thing of your brother’s, which he has lost and you have found. You may not hide yourself.
